ev.inf_summer_flux.title: The Summer Sickness
ev.inf_summer_flux.text: The heat has settled in, and for three days your bowels have run loose. You won't take the breast, your eyes have sunk, and your crying has gone quiet - which is worse than screaming. Your mother {npc} knows that in summer this sickness takes more babies than any other.
ev.inf_summer_flux.healer.success: The healer said to give you thin grain broth by the spoonful - little and often. Two days later you were nursing greedily again.
ev.inf_summer_flux.healer.failure: The healer left a bitter draught and took his fee. The sickness passed on its own a week later, and you stayed thin and pale for a long time.
ev.inf_summer_flux.breast: Keep you at the breast and give you water drop by drop
ev.inf_summer_flux.breast.success: {npc} didn't put you down for two days: the breast, a sip of water, the breast again. On the third morning you slept peacefully - and she fell asleep sitting up.
ev.inf_summer_flux.breast.failure: However much she gave you, it ran straight through. You pulled through, but there was little left of you but eyes.
ev.inf_summer_flux.pray.christian: Light a candle and pray for your health
ev.inf_summer_flux.pray.islamic: Recite verses of the Qur'an over you
ev.inf_summer_flux.pray.dharmic: Make a vow at the shrine and tie a blessed thread on your wrist
ev.inf_summer_flux.pray.east_asian: Bring offerings to the shrine and hang a charm over your bed
ev.inf_summer_flux.pray.polytheist: Make an offering to the healing gods
ev.inf_summer_flux.pray.mesoamerican: Burn copal before the gods and beg for mercy
ev.inf_summer_flux.pray.andean: Offer maize and coca leaves to the huaca
ev.inf_summer_flux.pray.african: Ask the ancestor spirits for protection
ev.inf_summer_flux.pray.success: By evening the sickness eased, and for the first time in three days you slept without crying. The household decided the prayers had been heard.
ev.inf_summer_flux.pray.failure: They prayed for three days, and for three days the sickness held on. You lived - but so weak you could barely hold up your head.
ev.inf_teething.title: Teething
ev.inf_teething.text: You're cutting teeth: red cheeks, a fever, you gnaw on everything within reach and cry the whole night through. Your mother {npc} hasn't slept in a week.
ev.inf_teething.gums: Rub your gums with honey and give you a smooth root to chew
ev.inf_teething.gums.success: The root beat any toy. The tooth came through, the fever went, and the house finally got some sleep.
ev.inf_teething.gums.failure: The fever climbed, and the runs came with it, as people say they do with teeth. For a week you were in a bad way.
ev.inf_teething.amulet.christian: Hang a little cross and a blessed medal round your neck
ev.inf_teething.amulet.islamic: Hang a pouch with a Qur'an verse round your neck
ev.inf_teething.amulet.jewish: Hang an amulet with holy names over the cradle
ev.inf_teething.amulet.dharmic: Tie a black thread with a charm on you
ev.inf_teething.amulet.east_asian: Hang a paper charm from the temple over your bed
ev.inf_teething.amulet.polytheist: Hang an amulet with the god's face round your neck
ev.inf_teething.amulet.mesoamerican: Tie a jade bead on a string around your wrist
ev.inf_teething.amulet.andean: Tie a charm on a llama-wool cord around you
ev.inf_teething.amulet.african: Tie a leather charm from the healer on you
ev.inf_teething.amulet.success: Charm or no charm, the tooth came through and you were smiling again.
ev.inf_teething.amulet.failure: The charm hung there and the fever stayed five more days. The tooth came through in the end - with a second one right behind it.
ev.inf_teething.healer.success: The healer said to rub your gums with oil and not to bundle you up in the fever. Three days later you were sleeping soundly.
ev.inf_teething.healer.failure: The healer bled the swollen gum - that was the cure in those days. It only weakened you, and the tooth came when it pleased.
ev.inf_whooping_cough.title: Whooping Cough
ev.inf_whooping_cough.text: You cough in fits - on and on until you turn blue, then drag in air with a whoop. The neighbours shake their heads: a cough like that lasts for months. Every night your mother {npc} holds you upright so you won't choke lying down.
ev.inf_whooping_cough.healer.success: The healer said to keep you warm but out in the fresh air and give you warm honeyed broth. The cough dragged on, but weaker every week.
ev.inf_whooping_cough.healer.failure: The healer came three times and was paid three times. The cough only left with the warm weather, and you gained no strength all that winter.
ev.inf_whooping_cough.steam: Hold you over the steam of hot herbs
ev.inf_whooping_cough.steam.success: Steam, honey and sleepless nights. Within a month the fits came less often, and then they stopped.
ev.inf_whooping_cough.steam.failure: The steam didn't help. The fits came a dozen a night, and you grew so weak you stopped even crying.
ev.inf_whooping_cough.pray.christian: Light a candle and pray for your health
ev.inf_whooping_cough.pray.islamic: Recite verses of the Qur'an over you
ev.inf_whooping_cough.pray.dharmic: Make a vow at the shrine and tie a blessed thread on your wrist
ev.inf_whooping_cough.pray.east_asian: Bring offerings to the shrine and hang a charm over your bed
ev.inf_whooping_cough.pray.polytheist: Make an offering to the healing gods
ev.inf_whooping_cough.pray.mesoamerican: Burn copal before the gods and beg for mercy
ev.inf_whooping_cough.pray.andean: Offer maize and coca leaves to the huaca
ev.inf_whooping_cough.pray.african: Ask the ancestor spirits for protection
ev.inf_whooping_cough.pray.success: Within a month the cough began to fade. Everyone in the house knew whom to thank.
ev.inf_whooping_cough.pray.failure: They prayed a long time, and the cough held on longer still - almost until spring.
ev.inf_measles.title: Measles
ev.inf_measles.text: Measles is going round: first the neighbours' children, now you - fever, red streaming eyes, a rash spreading down from your face. Your mother {npc} has seen measles empty whole streets of little ones.
ev.inf_measles.dark: Cover the windows, keep you in the half-dark and give you drink
ev.inf_measles.dark.success: For a week you lay in the half-dark. The rash darkened, peeled - and was gone. You got up thin but well.
ev.inf_measles.dark.failure: The rash faded, but a cough followed that hung on until the cold weather.
ev.inf_measles.healer.success: The physician said to shield your eyes from the light and give you barley water. On the tenth day you asked for food - and the whole house breathed out.
ev.inf_measles.healer.failure: The physician bled you, which only made things worse. The measles went, but the weakness stayed a long time.
ev.inf_measles.holy: Carry you to a holy place
ev.inf_measles.holy.christian: Carry you to a saint's relics
ev.inf_measles.holy.islamic: Carry you to a holy man's tomb
ev.inf_measles.holy.jewish: Carry you to the rabbi for a blessing
ev.inf_measles.holy.dharmic: Carry you to the temple to be sprinkled with holy water
ev.inf_measles.holy.east_asian: Carry you to the temple for a charm
ev.inf_measles.holy.polytheist: Carry you to the healing god's temple
ev.inf_measles.holy.mesoamerican: Carry you to the priest at the temple
ev.inf_measles.holy.andean: Carry you to the huaca on the hill
ev.inf_measles.holy.african: Carry you to the spirits' shrine
ev.inf_measles.holy.success: The journey there and back was hard on you, but by morning the fever broke. The family spoke of a miracle; the neighbours, of good strong stock.
ev.inf_measles.holy.failure: The journey wore you out, and the fever lasted another week. You recovered, but slowly.
ev.inf_smallpox.title: Smallpox
ev.inf_smallpox.text: Smallpox has come to the house. You are burning with fever, and blisters are rising on your skin. The grown-ups speak in whispers: it takes one sick child in three. Your mother {npc} never leaves your side.
ev.inf_smallpox.cool: Keep you cool and in the half-dark, and stop you scratching the sores
ev.inf_smallpox.cool.success: {npc} held your hands in hers day and night so you wouldn't scratch. The scabs fell away and left only a couple of pockmarks on your face.
ev.inf_smallpox.cool.failure: Two weeks between life and death. You pulled through, but the pockmarks on your face will stay for good.
ev.inf_smallpox.healer.success: The physician prescribed a sour draught and no heavy blankets. The fever broke on the ninth day, and you lived - with a mark or two to remember it by.
ev.inf_smallpox.healer.failure: The physician spread his hands and left. You lived all the same - pockmarked, and weak for a long time.
ev.inf_smallpox.pray.christian: Light a candle and pray for your health
ev.inf_smallpox.pray.islamic: Recite verses of the Qur'an over you
ev.inf_smallpox.pray.dharmic: Make a vow at the shrine and tie a blessed thread on your wrist
ev.inf_smallpox.pray.east_asian: Pray to the smallpox god and hang red cloth around the bed - the pox is said to fear it
ev.inf_smallpox.pray.polytheist: Make an offering to the healing gods
ev.inf_smallpox.pray.mesoamerican: Burn copal before the gods and beg for mercy
ev.inf_smallpox.pray.andean: Offer maize and coca leaves to the huaca
ev.inf_smallpox.pray.african: Ask the ancestor spirits for protection
ev.inf_smallpox.pray.hindu: Pray to Shitala, goddess of smallpox, and fan you with a neem branch
ev.inf_smallpox.pray.success: On the ninth day the fever retreated and the blisters dried. You lived, and the family gave thanks for it for a long time.
ev.inf_smallpox.pray.failure: They prayed day and night. You lived, but the pox left you a pitted face and a weak chest.
ev.inf_smallpox_new.title: The New Sickness
ev.inf_smallpox_new.text: Since the strangers came there has been a sickness no one here had ever known: fever, then pustules over the whole body. It goes from house to house, sparing neither lords nor commoners. Now you have it. Your mother {npc} can barely stand herself.
ev.inf_smallpox_new.healer.success: The healer gave you herbal brews and kept you from scratching. You lived - one of the few children on your street who did.
ev.inf_smallpox_new.healer.failure: The healer fell sick himself the next day. You pulled through without him - pockmarked and weak.
ev.inf_smallpox_new.care: Give you water, sponge you, and never leave your side
ev.inf_smallpox_new.care.success: {npc} sponged you, gave you water from her palm and kept the flies away. Many died then simply because no one was left to tend them. Someone tended you.
ev.inf_smallpox_new.care.failure: You lived, but the sickness took so much strength from you that you had to learn to walk all over again.
ev.inf_smallpox_new.pray.christian: Carry you to the new priests for their prayers
ev.inf_smallpox_new.pray.islamic: Recite verses of the Qur'an over you
ev.inf_smallpox_new.pray.dharmic: Make a vow at the shrine and tie a blessed thread on your wrist
ev.inf_smallpox_new.pray.east_asian: Bring offerings to the shrine and hang a charm over your bed
ev.inf_smallpox_new.pray.polytheist: Make an offering to the healing gods
ev.inf_smallpox_new.pray.mesoamerican: Burn copal before the gods and beg for mercy
ev.inf_smallpox_new.pray.andean: Offer maize and coca leaves to the huaca
ev.inf_smallpox_new.pray.african: Ask the ancestor spirits for protection
ev.inf_smallpox_new.pray.success: The fever broke on the tenth day. All around, neighbours were being buried, and you lay there asking for food.
ev.inf_smallpox_new.pray.failure: They prayed as long as they had strength. You lived, but your face would be pitted forever.
ev.inf_eye_sore.title: Sore Eyes
ev.inf_eye_sore.text: Your eyes are crusted shut with pus, the lids swollen; you rub them with your fists and cry at the light. Your mother {npc} is frightened: she has seen blind people whose trouble started just like this.
ev.inf_eye_sore.healer.ANE: Send for the physician with his eye salve
ev.inf_eye_sore.healer.ISL: Send for the kahhal, the eye doctor
ev.inf_eye_sore.healer.success: The doctor washed your eyes with a decoction and left a salve. A week later you were seeing the world clearly again.
ev.inf_eye_sore.healer.failure: The salve stung, and your eyes ran for another month. Your sight came back, but your left eye has been weaker ever since.
ev.inf_eye_sore.milk: Drip breast milk into your eyes, as everyone does
ev.inf_eye_sore.milk.success: Milk, warm compresses, a dark corner. In ten days the pus was gone.
ev.inf_eye_sore.milk.failure: Your eyes festered a long while. You recovered, but you've squinted at the sun ever since.
ev.inf_eye_sore.wash: Rinse your eyes with clean water and wait
ev.inf_eye_sore.wash.ANE: Line your eyes with kohl - it guards against eye sickness
ev.inf_eye_sore.wash.ISL: Line your eyes with kohl - it guards against eye sickness
ev.inf_eye_sore.wash.IND: Line your eyes with kajal - it guards against eye sickness
ev.inf_eye_sore.wash.success: A week later your eyes opened and stayed open.
ev.inf_eye_sore.wash.failure: Your eyes festered another month, and you were afraid of the light for a long time.
ev.inf_worms.title: Worms
ev.inf_worms.text: You eat and eat but don't grow: your belly is swollen, there are shadows under your eyes, and you grind your teeth at night. Your mother {npc} knows what it is - half the children around have the same.
ev.inf_worms.healer.success: The healer gave you a bitter purge. That day was dreadful, but a month later you were round and rosy.
ev.inf_worms.healer.failure: The purge didn't clear them all. For a long time you stayed the smallest among children your age.
ev.inf_worms.herbs: Dose you with bitter wormwood tea, the old women's way
ev.inf_worms.herbs.MAY: Dose you with bitter epazote tea, the old women's way
ev.inf_worms.herbs.AMR: Dose you with bitter epazote tea, the old women's way
ev.inf_worms.herbs.success: The bitterness stayed in your mouth for a week, but the bellyache stopped and you started to grow.
ev.inf_worms.herbs.failure: You spat out every other dose. The worms stayed, and with them the pallor and the endless tiredness.
ev.inf_worms.wait: Do nothing - you'll grow out of it
ev.inf_worms.wait.success: And so it went: by spring the belly trouble passed on its own. Lucky.
ev.inf_worms.wait.failure: It didn't pass. For a whole year you were listless and pale, until a neighbour pressed some bitter herbs on the family.
ev.inf_earache.title: Earache
ev.inf_earache.text: You scream and rub at your ear and won't let anyone touch it, and by nightfall the fever starts. Your mother {npc} rocks you by the fire, wondering what to do.
ev.inf_earache.warm: Warm your ear with a hot stone wrapped in cloth
ev.inf_earache.warm.success: Warmth and rocking did the trick: you fell asleep by morning, and in three days the ear stopped hurting.
ev.inf_earache.warm.failure: Towards morning the ear began to run. The pain went, but you never heard as well on that side again.
ev.inf_earache.healer.success: The healer put some pungent drops in your ear and said to keep you warm. A week later you had forgotten it ever hurt.
ev.inf_earache.healer.failure: The drops didn't help. The ear ached for two weeks, and the sleepless nights left you thin.
ev.inf_earache.pray.christian: Light a candle and pray for your health
ev.inf_earache.pray.islamic: Recite verses of the Qur'an over you
ev.inf_earache.pray.dharmic: Make a vow at the shrine and tie a blessed thread on your wrist
ev.inf_earache.pray.east_asian: Bring offerings to the shrine and hang a charm over your bed
ev.inf_earache.pray.polytheist: Make an offering to the healing gods
ev.inf_earache.pray.mesoamerican: Burn copal before the gods and beg for mercy
ev.inf_earache.pray.andean: Offer maize and coca leaves to the huaca
ev.inf_earache.pray.african: Ask the ancestor spirits for protection
ev.inf_earache.pray.success: Just before dawn the pain suddenly let go, and you fell asleep in her arms. The household took it as a sign.
ev.inf_earache.pray.failure: The pain lasted another week. The ear healed on its own, but your hearing was noticeably duller after.
ev.inf_rash.title: The Itch
ev.inf_rash.text: Tiny red spots have broken out between your fingers and across your belly. You scratch till you bleed and can't sleep at night. Your mother {npc} has washed everything in the house, but the itch won't go.
ev.inf_rash.wash: Wash you in ash-lye and rub you with herb salve
ev.inf_rash.wash.success: The lye stung and you howled, but within a week your skin was clear.
ev.inf_rash.wash.failure: The salve didn't help, and the scratches festered. Your skin only healed when the cold came.
ev.inf_rash.healer.success: The healer gave a sharp-smelling ointment and said to steam all the clothes and bedding. The itch was gone in a few days.
ev.inf_rash.healer.failure: The ointment burned, and the itch kept coming back. It was two months before you stopped scratching.
ev.inf_rash.wait: Put up with it - it'll pass
ev.inf_rash.wait.success: It did pass on its own - not quickly, but it passed.
ev.inf_rash.wait.failure: It didn't pass. The scratches got infected, and you ran a fever for a week.
ev.inf_hearth_burn.title: Burned
ev.inf_hearth_burn.text: You reached the hearth and grabbed a hot pot. Your palm rose in blisters, and the whole street must have heard you scream. Your mother {npc} snatched you up.
ev.inf_hearth_burn.cold: Plunge your hand in cold water, then dress it with honey
ev.inf_hearth_burn.cold.success: Cold water, honey, a clean cloth. Two weeks later all that was left was a pink spot - and a healthy respect for fire.
ev.inf_hearth_burn.cold.failure: The burn festered. The hand healed, but it left a scar on your palm, and for a long time you couldn't make a fist.
ev.inf_hearth_burn.healer.success: The healer put on a salve dressing and said to change it daily. The hand healed clean.
ev.inf_hearth_burn.healer.failure: The dressing stuck fast, and taking it off was torture. The hand healed, but the scar stayed.
ev.inf_hearth_burn.grease: Smear it with fat and bind it up, the way it's always been done
ev.inf_hearth_burn.grease.success: Fat, a rag and patience. The hand healed, if slowly.
ev.inf_hearth_burn.grease.failure: Under the grease the burn turned angry, and you ran a fever for days. The scar stayed for life.
ev.inf_fall.title: A Fall
ev.inf_fall.text: You climbed where no one ever let you go, and fell. You aren't crying - and that is the most frightening thing of all. Your father {npc} was the first to reach you.
ev.inf_fall.text.ANE: In summer the whole family sleeps on the flat roof, and in the night you crawled to the very edge - and fell into the courtyard. You aren't crying - and that is the most frightening thing of all. Your father {npc} was first down the ladder to you.
ev.inf_fall.text.ISL: In summer the whole family sleeps on the flat roof, and in the night you crawled to the very edge - and fell into the courtyard. You aren't crying - and that is the most frightening thing of all. Your father {npc} was first down the ladder to you.
ev.inf_fall.text.IND: In summer the whole family sleeps on the flat roof, and in the night you crawled to the very edge - and fell into the courtyard. You aren't crying - and that is the most frightening thing of all. Your father {npc} was first down the ladder to you.
ev.inf_fall.text.WAF: In summer the whole family sleeps on the flat roof, and in the night you crawled to the very edge - and fell into the courtyard. You aren't crying - and that is the most frightening thing of all. Your father {npc} was first down the ladder to you.
ev.inf_fall.bonesetter.success: The bonesetter felt every bone, put your shoulder back in place and ordered rest. A month later you were climbing where you shouldn't again.
ev.inf_fall.bonesetter.failure: The bonesetter bound the arm tight, but it knitted crooked. You'll get used to it.
ev.inf_fall.watch.success: At last you started to bawl - and your father breathed again. You got off with a lump and some bruises.
ev.inf_fall.watch.failure: For a long time you were listless and sick, and your head ached for days. Your father never left you unwatched again.
ev.inf_fall.pray.christian: Light a candle and pray for your health
ev.inf_fall.pray.islamic: Recite verses of the Qur'an over you
ev.inf_fall.pray.dharmic: Make a vow at the shrine and tie a blessed thread on your wrist
ev.inf_fall.pray.east_asian: Bring offerings to the shrine and hang a charm over your bed
ev.inf_fall.pray.polytheist: Make an offering to the healing gods
ev.inf_fall.pray.mesoamerican: Burn copal before the gods and beg for mercy
ev.inf_fall.pray.andean: Offer maize and coca leaves to the huaca
ev.inf_fall.pray.african: Ask the ancestor spirits for protection
ev.inf_fall.pray.success: While he prayed, you opened your eyes and demanded food. Nothing worse than bruises.
ev.inf_fall.pray.failure: The bruises faded, but the headaches stayed for months.
ev.inf_scorpion.title: Scorpion
ev.inf_scorpion.text: A scorpion was hiding in the folds of the bedding and stung you on the leg. The leg swells, you shriek, and then you begin to shake. Your mother {npc} crushed the creature with a sandal - but what now?
ev.inf_scorpion.charmer: Send for the healer who treats stings
ev.inf_scorpion.charmer.thebes: Send for the scorpion charmer from the temple of Serket
ev.inf_scorpion.charmer.memphis: Send for the scorpion charmer from the temple of Serket
ev.inf_scorpion.charmer.babylon: Send for the ashipu, the exorcist
ev.inf_scorpion.charmer.assur: Send for the ashipu, the exorcist
ev.inf_scorpion.charmer.success: He washed the sting, gave you a bitter brew and chanted over you till morning. By dawn the shaking had stopped.
ev.inf_scorpion.charmer.failure: Your leg swelled to the knee, and you lay two days in a fever. Then it eased.
ev.inf_scorpion.cut: Cut the sting and suck out the venom
ev.inf_scorpion.cut.success: {npc} spat and held you close. The swelling went down by evening.
ev.inf_scorpion.cut.failure: The cut festered, and the venom did its work anyway: three days of fever.
ev.inf_scorpion.pray.christian: Light a candle and pray for your health
ev.inf_scorpion.pray.islamic: Recite verses of the Qur'an over you
ev.inf_scorpion.pray.dharmic: Make a vow at the shrine and tie a blessed thread on your wrist
ev.inf_scorpion.pray.east_asian: Bring offerings to the shrine and hang a charm over your bed
ev.inf_scorpion.pray.polytheist: Make an offering to the healing gods
ev.inf_scorpion.pray.mesoamerican: Burn copal before the gods and beg for mercy
ev.inf_scorpion.pray.andean: Offer maize and coca leaves to the huaca
ev.inf_scorpion.pray.african: Ask the ancestor spirits for protection
ev.inf_scorpion.pray.success: You shook all night, and by morning it passed. The scorpion must have been a small one - or the prayer a strong one.
ev.inf_scorpion.pray.failure: {npc} watched you toss in fever for three days. You came through - but she went grey in those days.
ev.inf_snakebite.title: Snakebite
ev.inf_snakebite.text: You were playing at the edge of the field when a snake struck from the grass. Two red dots on your ankle. Your father {npc} came running at your scream and saw it slither away.
ev.inf_snakebite.healer.IND: Run for the visha-vaidya, the poison healer
ev.inf_snakebite.healer.success: The healer knew the snake from the description and said it had little venom in it. A brew, a poultice, a charm - and three days later you were running about.
ev.inf_snakebite.healer.failure: Your leg went black to the knee. The healer sat with you four nights. You lived, but you limped until autumn.
ev.inf_snakebite.tie: Bind your leg tight and cut the wound
ev.inf_snakebite.tie.success: Your father tied off the leg with a cord, cut the wound and squeezed out the blood. The leg swelled, but by morning it was going down.
ev.inf_snakebite.tie.failure: The leg swelled, the cut festered, and you lay a week in fever.
ev.inf_snakebite.pray.christian: Light a candle and pray for your health
ev.inf_snakebite.pray.islamic: Recite verses of the Qur'an over you
ev.inf_snakebite.pray.dharmic: Make a vow at the shrine and tie a blessed thread on your wrist
ev.inf_snakebite.pray.east_asian: Bring offerings to the shrine and hang a charm over your bed
ev.inf_snakebite.pray.polytheist: Make an offering to the healing gods
ev.inf_snakebite.pray.mesoamerican: Burn copal before the gods and beg for mercy
ev.inf_snakebite.pray.andean: Offer maize and coca leaves to the huaca
ev.inf_snakebite.pray.african: Ask the ancestor spirits for protection
ev.inf_snakebite.pray.success: The leg swelled and went down again, and you cried yourself to sleep. The snake must have bitten "dry".
ev.inf_snakebite.pray.failure: For three days you burned with fever and the leg turned black. You lived - barely.
ev.inf_marsh_fever.title: Marsh Fever
ev.inf_marsh_fever.text: Damp drifts up from the river, and the mosquitoes whine at dusk. You shake with chills, then burn, then shake again - every other day. Your mother {npc} knows this fever: it comes back.
ev.inf_marsh_fever.healer.success: The physician prescribed a bitter draught at the hour of the chills. The fits grew shorter, and within a month they stopped.
ev.inf_marsh_fever.healer.failure: The fever retreated but never quite left: for two more years it came back every summer.
ev.inf_marsh_fever.herbs.CHN: Give you qinghao, sweet wormwood tea
ev.inf_marsh_fever.herbs.success: The brew was so bitter you wailed after every spoonful. But the fits stopped.
ev.inf_marsh_fever.herbs.failure: The herbs eased the fits but didn't drive them out. You grew up a pale little scrap of a thing.
ev.inf_marsh_fever.holy: Carry you to a holy place
ev.inf_marsh_fever.holy.christian: Carry you to a saint's relics
ev.inf_marsh_fever.holy.islamic: Carry you to a holy man's tomb
ev.inf_marsh_fever.holy.jewish: Carry you to the rabbi for a blessing
ev.inf_marsh_fever.holy.dharmic: Carry you to the temple to be sprinkled with holy water
ev.inf_marsh_fever.holy.east_asian: Carry you to the temple for a charm
ev.inf_marsh_fever.holy.polytheist: Carry you to the healing god's temple
ev.inf_marsh_fever.holy.mesoamerican: Carry you to the priest at the temple
ev.inf_marsh_fever.holy.andean: Carry you to the huaca on the hill
ev.inf_marsh_fever.holy.african: Carry you to the spirits' shrine
ev.inf_marsh_fever.holy.success: After that day the fits began to wane. Your mother took thank-offerings there for a long time after.
ev.inf_marsh_fever.holy.failure: It didn't help. The fever shook you till the cold weather and returned more than once.
ev.inf_bean_choke.title: Choking
ev.inf_bean_choke.text: You put a dry bean in your mouth - and it lodged in your throat. You can't breathe, can't cry, you're just turning blue. Your father {npc} was right there.
ev.inf_bean_choke.upside: Turn you upside down and thump your back
ev.inf_bean_choke.upside.success: Three thumps - and the bean shot out onto the floor. You bawled so loudly your father laughed with relief.
ev.inf_bean_choke.upside.failure: The bean didn't come out at once. For a week afterwards you croaked - your throat was raw.
ev.inf_bean_choke.finger: Try to hook it out with a finger
ev.inf_bean_choke.finger.success: {npc} hooked the bean out on the first try. Then he sat for a long time holding you, saying nothing.
ev.inf_bean_choke.finger.failure: His finger pushed the bean deeper. You coughed it up on your own when your father was at his wits' end. Your throat hurt for a week.
ev.inf_dog_bite.title: Dog Bite
ev.inf_dog_bite.text: A stranger's dog whose tail you pulled sank its teeth into your arm. The bite is deep and won't stop bleeding. Your father {npc} drove it off with a stick and now frowns over the wound: what if it's mad?
ev.inf_dog_bite.healer.success: The healer washed the wound, cauterized it and stitched it. The dog was seen alive and well afterwards - so it wasn't mad.
ev.inf_dog_bite.healer.failure: The wound festered, and you ran a fever for a week. The scar on your arm will be there forever.
ev.inf_dog_bite.sear: Wash the wound and sear it with an ember
ev.inf_dog_bite.sear.success: You screamed the street down, but the wound closed clean.
ev.inf_dog_bite.sear.failure: A burn on top of a bite, and both festered. You recovered, but with two scars instead of one.
ev.inf_dog_bite.hair: Bind the wound with hair from that very dog, as the old folk advise
ev.inf_dog_bite.hair.success: Dog hair, a rag, a charm. The wound closed up - nobody can say why.
ev.inf_dog_bite.hair.failure: The wound became inflamed and your arm swelled to the elbow. You lay a week in fever.
ev.inf_famine.title: The Hungry Year
ev.inf_famine.text: The harvest failed, and by spring there is almost nothing to eat in the house. You've gone quiet and listless - the way hungry children do. Your mother {npc} looks at you and knows she can't wait.
ev.inf_famine.alms: Go begging at the gates of the rich
ev.inf_famine.alms.islamic: Go to the mosque where alms are given out
ev.inf_famine.alms.jewish: Ask for help from the community's fund for the poor
ev.inf_famine.alms.dharmic: Go to the temple where the poor are fed
ev.inf_famine.alms.andean: Ask for grain from the royal storehouses
ev.inf_famine.alms.success: They gave little, but it was enough to last until the new shoots came up. You started grabbing at everything and laughing again.
ev.inf_famine.alms.failure: The handouts were small and not every day. You lived through that year, but you grew up shorter than other children your age.
ev.inf_famine.share: Give you every crumb and live on roots herself
ev.inf_famine.share.success: She grew so thin the neighbours didn't know her, but you made it to the next harvest.
ev.inf_famine.share.failure: She gave everything, and it was not enough. You lived, but the weakness stayed with you a long time.
ev.inf_famine.gather: Forage for anything edible in the waste ground and by the river
ev.inf_famine.gather.success: Wild greens, roots, snails - everything went into the pot. You survived on that broth and even grew a little.
ev.inf_famine.gather.failure: The wild greens twisted your belly, and you lay flat for a week.
ev.inf_wet_nurse_ill.title: The Wet Nurse Falls Ill
ev.inf_wet_nurse_ill.text: The wet nurse who has fed you since your first days is down with a fever, and her milk has dried up. You are screaming with hunger. Your mother {npc} has to decide how you will be fed.
ev.inf_wet_nurse_ill.new_nurse: Find a new wet nurse at once
ev.inf_wet_nurse_ill.new_nurse.success: A new one was found by evening - young, healthy, with her own baby at the breast. You fed as if you hadn't eaten in a week.
ev.inf_wet_nurse_ill.new_nurse.failure: The new wet nurse turned out to be unwell herself. You caught her sickness and were a long time recovering.
ev.inf_wet_nurse_ill.self: Nurse you herself, whatever custom says
ev.inf_wet_nurse_ill.self.success: The milk was slow to come, but it came. Ever since there has been a special bond between you.
ev.inf_wet_nurse_ill.self.failure: There was barely enough milk. You lived on it and on thin gruel, but you grew slowly.
ev.inf_wet_nurse_ill.pap: Feed you thin pap from a spoon
ev.inf_wet_nurse_ill.pap.success: Watery pap and endless patience. You got used to it, and your cheeks filled out again.
ev.inf_wet_nurse_ill.pap.failure: The pap gave you bellyaches, and you were a sickly little thing all that year.
ev.inf_m_first_steps.text: Your mother {npc} crouched three steps away and held out her arms. You took those three steps all on your own - and tumbled into her arms, laughing.
ev.inf_m_first_tooth.text: Your first tooth came through. Everyone in the house had to feel it with a finger, and every one of them pronounced it a strong one.
ev.inf_m_second_word.text: Nobody could quite make out your first word, but your second was perfectly clear: 'Give!' Your father {npc} laughed for a long time and said someone like that would never go hungry.
ev.inf_m_sibling_name.text: As soon as you could talk, you called for your {g=npc_sex:brother|sister} from dawn to dusk: '{npc}! {npc}!' {g=npc_sex:He|She} was so flattered {g=npc_sex:he|she} carried you all round the neighbourhood for a week.
ev.inf_m_swaddling.text: You were swaddled tight from head to toe: it was said to make the legs grow straight and the sleep sound. You grunted in protest - and fell asleep.
ev.inf_m_cradleboard.text: Two small boards were gently bound to your head. In a few months your brow will slope long and high - as beauty demands, and as, they say, the young maize god looks.
ev.inf_m_wet_nurse.text: You were nursed by a wet nurse - a sturdy, quiet woman with warm hands. You would only fall asleep on her lap, and the household teased about it.
ev.inf_m_lullaby.text: Every evening your mother {npc} sang the same song over the cradle - about a bird that flew across the river and came back. One day you'll forget the words. Never the tune.
ev.inf_m_evil_eye.text: When a neighbour admired you a little too long, a charm against the evil eye was tied to your wrist at once. Praising a baby out loud is asking for trouble - everyone knows that.
ev.inf_m_evil_eye.text.islamic: A tiny hamsa hand was hung round your neck, and anyone who praised you had to add 'mashallah' - so the evil eye wouldn't stick.
ev.inf_m_evil_eye.text.CHN: So the evil spirits would not covet you, at home you were called by a deliberately ugly pet name - "Puppy". Who would bother stealing a puppy?
ev.inf_m_evil_eye.text.IND: A black dot of kohl was put on your cheek - let the evil eye catch on the flaw and leave the rest of you alone.
ev.inf_m_evil_eye.text.RUS: So no one would cast the evil eye, for the first forty days you were hardly shown to anyone, and when neighbours praised you the answer was, 'Oh, it's a scrawny little thing.'
ev.inf_m_goose.text: In the yard a goose came at you, hissing and flapping - nearly as tall as you were. You fled bawling across the whole yard, and you've given geese a wide berth ever since.
ev.inf_m_goose.text.WAF: In the yard a rooster flew at you, flapping - a fierce one with a flaming comb. You fled bawling across the whole yard, and you've given roosters a wide berth ever since.
ev.inf_m_goose.text.ETH: In the yard a rooster flew at you, flapping - a fierce one with a flaming comb. You fled bawling across the whole yard, and you've given roosters a wide berth ever since.
ev.inf_m_goose.text.IND: In the yard a rooster flew at you, flapping - a fierce one with a flaming comb. You fled bawling across the whole yard, and you've given roosters a wide berth ever since.
ev.inf_m_hearth_ash.text: While nobody was looking you crawled into the cold ash by the hearth and came out grey from head to toe. The whole household scrubbed you down while you shrieked with laughter.
ev.inf_m_lost_market.text: At the market you got caught staring at a man selling caged birds and let go of the hem you were holding. When your mother {npc} found you, she hugged you tight first - and smacked you after.
ev.inf_m_old_tale.text: The old woman next door, who had neither teeth nor kin left, told you by the fire how the world is made: who holds up the sky, where thunder comes from, where the dead go. You understood half and remembered all of it.
ev.inf_m_sibling_jealous.text: At first your {g=npc_sex:brother|sister} {npc} resented you: since you arrived, nobody fussed over anyone else. Once {g=npc_sex:he|she} pinched you - and when you burst into tears, {g=npc_sex:he|she} got frightened and scrambled to comfort you.
ev.inf_m_shoulders.text: Your father {npc} lifted you onto his shoulders, and suddenly the world was enormous: rooftops, hearth smoke, a road running to the very edge of the earth. You clung to his hair and refused to come down.
ev.inf_m_famine_year.text: You were born in a hungry year, when the old folk ate every other day so the children would have enough. They say you were fed soaked flatbread from someone's palm - and lived, out of sheer stubbornness.
ev.inf_m_good_harvest.text: The year you were born brought a fine harvest: full storehouses, feasts that ran late into the night. The neighbours decided you'd brought the luck with you, and called you their harvest child for years.
ev.inf_m_guard_dog.text: The yard dog, uninvited, lay down beside your cradle and from then on growled at anyone who came too close too fast. Even family.
ev.inf_m_first_festival.text: For the first time you were taken to a great festival: drums, fires, crowds, the smell of roasting meat. You fell asleep in someone's arms, a sweet still clutched in your fist.
ev.inf_m_thunderstorm.text: One night a storm broke so hard the walls shook. You burrowed under the blanket, and one of the grown-ups sat up till dawn telling you it was only the sky grumbling.
ev.inf_m_first_fruit.text: You were given your first ripe fruit - so soft and sweet the juice ran down your chin and arms. You demanded more at once.
ev.inf_m_first_fruit.text.E03: You were given a ripe fig for the first time. The juice ran down your chin and arms, and you demanded more at once.
ev.inf_m_first_fruit.text.ANE: You were given a ripe date for the first time. The juice ran down your chin and arms, and you demanded more at once.
ev.inf_m_first_fruit.text.BYZ: You were given a bunch of sweet grapes for the first time. The juice ran down your chin and arms, and you demanded more at once.
ev.inf_m_first_fruit.text.ISL: You were given your first pomegranate. You got crimson juice up to your ears and scattered seeds all over the floor. You demanded more at once.
ev.inf_m_first_fruit.text.CHN: You were given a ripe peach for the first time. The juice ran down your chin and arms, and you demanded more at once.
ev.inf_m_first_fruit.text.JPN: You were given a ripe persimmon for the first time. The juice ran down your chin and arms, and you demanded more at once.
ev.inf_m_first_fruit.text.IND: You were given a ripe banana for the first time. The juice ran down your chin and arms, and you demanded more at once.
ev.inf_m_first_fruit.text.EUR: You were given a handful of ripe cherries for the first time. The juice ran down your chin and arms, and you demanded more at once.
ev.inf_m_first_fruit.text.RUS: You were given a handful of wild strawberries for the first time. The juice ran down your chin and arms, and you demanded more at once.
ev.inf_m_first_fruit.text.WAF: You were given the pulp of a shea fruit, sweet as honey for the first time. The juice ran down your chin and arms, and you demanded more at once.
ev.inf_m_first_fruit.text.MAY: You were given a ripe sapote for the first time. The juice ran down your chin and arms, and you demanded more at once.
ev.inf_m_first_fruit.text.AMR: You were given a ripe tuna - a cactus fruit with the spines scraped off for the first time. The juice ran down your chin and arms, and you demanded more at once.
ev.inf_m_first_fruit.text.cusco: You were given a ripe cherimoya for the first time. The juice ran down your chin and arms, and you demanded more at once.
ev.inf_m_first_fruit.text.quito: You were given a ripe cherimoya for the first time. The juice ran down your chin and arms, and you demanded more at once.
ev.inf_m_carried_back.text: Your mother {npc} worked the fields with you tied to her back in a cloth. Your whole first year passed to the rhythm of her swaying, her breathing, and the songs she hummed under her breath.
ev.inf_m_carried_back.text.RUS: Your mother {npc} went out to the fields for the whole day and laid you in a cradle hung from a pole at the edge of the strip. Your whole first year passed to the rustle of the grain and her calls from afar: "Sleep now, sleep…"
ev.inf_m_nursemaid.text: You were looked after by a nursemaid - an unfree woman brought long ago from far away. She sang to you in a language no one else in the house knew, and those songs put you to sleep better than any others.
ev.inf_m_annaprashana.text: In your sixth month came your annaprashana, the first rice-feeding. You were dressed in new clothes and given a pinch of rice cooked in sweet milk. You screwed up your face - then reached for more.
ev.inf_m_aqiqah.text: On your seventh day you were named and your head was shaved; the hair was weighed and its weight in silver given to the poor. This was the aqiqa - your welcome into the community.
ev.inf_m_rattle.text: You had a rattle - a hollow clay ball with pebbles inside. You shook it from dawn to dusk, and the household's patience was wearing thin.
